recipes.name: Chef John's Chicken and Mushrooms
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste
8 ounces fresh mushrooms, sliced 1/4 inch thick
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Season chicken on all sides with salt and ground black pepper.
Heat olive oil over medium-high heat in an ovenproof skillet. Place chicken skin-side down in skillet and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Turn chicken over; stir mushrooms with a pinch of salt into skillet. Increase heat to high; cook, stirring mushrooms occasionally, until mushrooms shrink slightly, about 5 minutes.

Transfer skillet to the preheated oven and cook until chicken is no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, 15 to 20 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Transfer chicken breasts to a plate and loosely tent with foil; set aside.

Set skillet on the stovetop over medium-high heat; cook and stir mushrooms until brown bits start to form on the bottom of the pan, about 5 minutes. Pour water into the skillet, and bring to a boil while scraping the browned bits off of the bottom of the pan. Cook until water is reduced by half, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Stir in any accumulated juices from the chicken into the skillet. Stir butter into mushroom mixture, stirring constantly until butter is completely melted and incorporated.
Season with salt and pepper. Spoon mushroom sauce over chicken and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John's Chicken and Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: Succulent chicken breasts topped with perfectly sauteed mushrooms create a delicious, yet very simple, dish.

review.reviewBody: A great simple recipe. I made it with boneless skinless chicken breasts and added a chopped onion for a bit more flavor, but I'm sure it would be just as good as directed. Thanks!

I followed this recipe to the T, and it came out delicious! It was simple, quick, and had only a few main ingredients so I didn't have to go to the store to get anything off hand. It also still tasted good when I reheated it for lunch. I think next time I may add in some onions, just for some more flavor, but it was delicious!

Got this recipe from a top NY chef with one twist: rub skin side with your favorite pork/chicken rub ( grab one from the store-Stonewall great) then sprinkle on other side when chick is skin down. Fab favor and sauce. PS olive oil not needed as skin produces lots of rendered fat.-Drain excess when you turn chick in pan.
But if you have on hand scallions and garlic, don't hesitate to add them just before the chicken. A little white wine is good to add just before transferring to the oven
Practically perfect. Try this...delete the salt, put a chicken bullion cube in the water and heat it first, then add 3 tablespoons of Marsala wine.

I broke one of my long-time rules ......... I modified it a bit (based on reviews) before making it the first time ......... shame, shame. But, it is a GREAT canvas to create a tasty and easy meal. My mods were: 1/4 c each of broth and white wine instead of water, a sprinkle of Hungarian Paprika, a tbsp. of chopped onion, and a small clove of garlic chopped. Served over brown rice made a tasty meal. Thanks, again, Chef John.

I took other reviewer's advice and added thinly sliced onions with the mushrooms, then slivered garlic during the last minute. Then, instead of water, I used 1/2 white wine and reduced by half, then added 1/2 cup of chicken broth and reduced that by half. Served with steamed asparagus and buttered egg noodles. My husband said "I don't know what you did to the mushrooms, but they are wonderful!"

This was FANTASTIC! An amazing start to a recipe. I used one chicken breast and 2 thighs (not boneless skinless), which I seasoned liberally with Penzeys Northwoods seasoning and garlic salt. I chopped a large onion and added that to the chicken at the beginning. I sauteed about 7-8 minutes due to the thighs with bones. Then I flipped the chicken over and added the mushrooms and sauteed another 7-8 minutes before putting in the oven for 20 minutes. Then I removed the chicken and added 1/2 cup chicken broth and 1/2 cup white wine plus a little cayenne and 2 T butter instead of 1. I served it with wild rice, and the extra liquid made enough amazing gravy to also cover the rice. This looked GORGEOUS on the plate and tasted AMAZING! Thank you John!

My family (especially my husband) aren't huge fans of classic American stroganof. This hit the spot for me and was something every single person in my family liked. We did boneless and skinless chicken and it still turned out great. We have a Meater thermometer (I inserted right before putting the cast iron pan in the oven) and it helped us have super juicy, perfectly cooked chicken. I also chopped the mushrooms up pretty small because my kids like mushrooms but only if they're tiny. We served over egg noodles. I highly recommend this recipe!

Here are a few changes to consider: 1. add bacon- because everything, especially chicken breast, will taste better;2. pound out those chicken breasts- otherwise, the chicken meat will cook unevenly (this is basic chicken breast cooking 101, IMO!); 3. use a white wine or a chicken stock to de-glaze- the flavor of the "sauce" will increase by more than a few Emeril notches over using only water; 4. one last idea- add a 1/2 tsp of your favorite mustard to the sauce! You must be bold and daring to try this step, but c'mon, give it a try!
good meal- added wine ilo water and use garlic and onions with mushrooms
I always look for Chef John's recipes! They are the BESTEST!

The sauce was very watery. I added some cornstarch and water, then gravy master. Other than salt and pepper, it had little taste. If I do try it again, I will add garlic and maybe some smoked paprika. I wasn't terrible, just lacked flavor.
Instead of water, I added flavor with lemon zest and white wine. A also added garlic powder to salt & pepper seasoning. Results were spectacular.
I’ve made this numerous times over the past couple of years. Always turns out great.
This is easy and good, but I used chicken broth instead of water and sprinkled some garlic powder on the mushrooms when sauteing .
If I run out of mushrooms I substitute with sweet onions. Just as delicious!!!

I have made it 2 or 3 times with 3 chicken breast halves, adjusting oil, mushrooms, and butter accordingly, but following recipe exactly otherwise. I have to go to a farmers' market to get boneless, skin-on chicken breasts, which I can't always do. Since so many reviewers mention good results with skinless, I may give that a try. I have homemade chicken broth in the freezer so I might use that instead of water and someone mentioned onion and garlic, which also sounds appealing. But as written and demonstrated by Chef John, it is awesome.
Perfect. No notes.
Very salty and yet tasteless. It didn’t work as a recipe. Did not like it. Sorry
